question: True or false: a painting whose canvas, ground and pigments all test as seventeenth-century can still be modern?
answer: True. Materials can prove a painting too young, never old enough. Old canvases, old panels and period pigments can all be bought: Han van Meegeren acquired minor seventeenth-century paintings, scraped them down and painted his Vermeers on the genuine canvas. A clean result from a materials test only means the forger made no mistake there.
move: A test that can only say no cannot say yes.
ask: Which of my beliefs has only passed tests that could never have proved it wrong?
trap: Treating a passed test as proof, not as the absence of disproof.
source: Lopez, The Man Who Made Vermeers, 2008
reference: Jonathan Lopez, The Man Who Made Vermeers: Unvarnishing the Legend of Master Forger Han van Meegeren, Harcourt, 2008
